overview: This single-page file index concerns motion-picture distribution in the Kwantung Leased Territory, particularly Dairen, and lists four reports sent by Grummon to the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo. The listed papers address difficulties faced by American film distributors, a contemplated American distributors’ association, and a projected monopoly over film distribution in Manchuria; one report enclosed a translated article from the February 1937 issue of KEIZAI MANCHU (ECONOMIC MANCHURIA). Three entries are cross-referenced to the Manchuria motion-pictures file, 893.4061.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: Motion Pictures—Kwantung Leased Territory
subfiles.about: An index lists four reports from Grummon at Dairen to the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo concerning American film distributors and a proposed motion-picture distribution monopoly in Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: The index records a December 2 report on difficulties confronting American film distributors in Dairen and their contemplated formation of an association. Three further entries, dated February 16, March 11, and February 23, concern reports of a projected monopoly over motion-picture film distribution in Manchuria. The February 23 entry notes an enclosed translation from the February 1937 issue of KEIZAI MANCHU (ECONOMIC MANCHURIA), said to confirm the monopoly report. The monopoly-related papers are cross-referenced to file 893.4061-Motion Pictures-Manchuria.

interest: The page is useful as a compact map of diplomatic reporting on attempts to regulate or monopolize film distribution in Japanese-controlled Manchuria and on the collective response contemplated by American businesses. It also identifies a Japanese-period economic publication used as corroborating evidence and points researchers to the related Manchuria decimal file. Notably, the surviving page is headed “MOTION PICTURES,” despite the supplied file title identifying the particular subject as “Concert,” suggesting a cataloguing or filing inconsistency worth investigating.
